chunks: From him, from ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Ṣafwān, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
If you do not know how much you have prayed, and your conjecture does not settle upon anything, then repeat the salat (prayer).

key_terms.كَمْ صَلَّيْتَ: how much of the prayer you have performed
key_terms.لَا تَدْرِي: you do not know or are uncertain

ai.seo_question: What should you do if you completely forget how many rakʿahs you have prayed and have no probable assumption?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes uncertain about the number of rakʿahs prayed and has no prevailing assumption. In such a case, the person is instructed to repeat the salat (prayer). It is significant in Shia fiqh for rulings on doubt in prayer.
